exhibits.title: The Conditioning Cauldron — adaLN-Zero
exhibits.text:
A DiT block is almost the ordinary Transformer block from the Attention wing's Library of Keys: attention → residual → MLP → residual. It changes only how it LISTENS. The new problem is CONDITIONING — the block must be told two things at every step: the timestep t (WHICH noise level it is denoising) and the class-or-text c (WHAT to generate). This cauldron is where that telling happens.

First, the two signals are MERGED. The timestep is spun into t_embed by the sinusoidal ladder of the basement Wheel of Frequencies — the very same freq_i = 1/10000^(2i/d) construction that gives tokens their positional 'where' now gives the denoiser its 'which step.' The condition c is turned into c_embed. Because both live in the SAME d-dimensional space, they are simply SUMMED into one vector — exactly as a token embedding and a positional embedding are added upstairs. The result is a single 'this noise level AND this prompt' signal:
  cond = t_embed + c_embed

Second, that merged signal is poured through a small MLP that EMITS the block's adaptive parameters — a full set per sub-layer:
  cond → MLP → (γ₁, β₁, α₁)  for the attention sub-layer
              (γ₂, β₂, α₂)  for the MLP sub-layer

These are not fixed learned constants. They are GENERATED afresh for every (t, c). That is the whole idea of adaptive LayerNorm — adaLN.

The block then flows, with x of shape (256 tokens, d):
  x → adaLN(x; γ₁, β₁) → self-attention → ×α₁ → + x
    → adaLN(x; γ₂, β₂) → MLP          → ×α₂ → + x
where adaLN(x; γ, β) = γ · normalize(x) + β, the same LN formula but with γ, β arriving from the conditioning rather than baked into the weights.

Two differences from the standard block, and only two:
  (1) LN → adaLN: the scale γ and shift β are now FUNCTIONS of (t, c), not frozen constants.
  (2) A gate α multiplies each residual branch before it rejoins the highway — an extra dial the standard block does not have.

The '-Zero' is the trick that makes deep DiTs trainable: the MLP that emits α is initialised so that every α STARTS AT ZERO. With α₁ = α₂ = 0, each branch contributes ×0 — nothing — so the block is pure identity through its residual (x → x). At the first step of training a hundred-block transformer is a clean pass-through, no exploding signal. Training then gradually TURNS EACH BLOCK ON by learning nonzero α, so depth is switched in slowly rather than fought from the start.

A note the sanctum keeps carved by the door: t is ALWAYS present — every reverse step has a timestep. c is SWAPPABLE — a class embedding, a text-encoder's output, or null. That null pass is not a special mode; it is exactly the unconditional branch of Classifier-Free Guidance forged in the Diffusion wing's Guidance Forge. Same cauldron, one flame with the prompt, one with ∅.

exhibits.title: The Frozen Dial and the Poured Dial
exhibits.text: Normal LayerNorm carries two dials: LN(x) = γ · normalize(x) + β. It first standardises x — subtract the mean, divide by the standard deviation, so each token's features have zero mean and unit variance — then rescales by a learned γ and shifts by a learned β. Crucially, γ and β are FIXED after training: two frozen numbers per feature, identical for every input the model ever sees. adaLN keeps the exact same formula but UNFREEZES the dials. Instead of storing γ and β in the weights, the block GENERATES them from the conditioning: cond → MLP → γ, β. Now the normalisation adapts — a high-noise timestep can ask for one scale-and-shift, a low-noise one for another, and a 'cat' prompt for a different feature emphasis than a 'cathedral' prompt. The normalize step is unchanged; only where γ and β COME FROM has moved, from the frozen weights to the poured conditioning.

exhibits.title: Why t and c Are Added, Not Concatenated
exhibits.text: It looks careless to ADD the timestep embedding and the condition embedding into one vector — surely 'which noise level' and 'which prompt' are different questions? But this is the same move as the original transformer adding a token embedding to a positional embedding. Both t_embed and c_embed are constructed to inhabit the SAME d-dimensional space, and summing there produces a single fused signal — 'denoise AT this level, TOWARD this thing' — that the downstream MLP reads as one instruction. It is not 't makes its own γ and c makes another'; they merge FIRST, then one shared MLP emits one set of γ, β, α. The network learns to disentangle what it needs from the sum, exactly as it learns to read 'this word HERE' from an added position. The timestep half is built by the basement Wheel of Frequencies: t is spun through the sinusoidal frequencies freq_i = 1/10000^(2i/d) into a rich fingerprint of which step — the identical machinery that fixes a token's position upstairs, wearing a third costume down here as timestep embedding.

exhibits.title: The Gate That Starts Shut
exhibits.text: Why initialise α to zero? Picture stacking a hundred blocks and letting each one write its full, randomly-initialised opinion onto the residual highway at step one of training — the signal blows up or thrashes, and deep transformers become miserable to train. The α gate is a valve on each residual branch: output = x + α · branch(x). Set α = 0 and the branch is silenced, so the block reduces to output = x, a perfect identity — every block passes its input through untouched. A freshly-born DiT of any depth is therefore a clean, stable pass-through: gradients flow straight down the residual, nothing explodes. From there, training LEARNS the α's up from zero, gently opening one gate at a time, so the model earns its depth instead of paying for it all at once. This is what the 'Zero' in adaLN-Zero names — not the γ or β, but the α gates that begin shut. It is the residual-highway idea of the Library of Keys given a dimmer switch, defaulted to off.

exhibits.caption: Standard block, two edits: LN→adaLN (γ,β poured from t+c) and a gate α on each residual. α starts at zero, so a newborn block is pure identity (x→x) and the network turns its depth on by learning α upward.

exhibits.title: The Cauldron's Dials, Poured and Gated
exhibits.caption: The cauldron traced in full. Panel (a): the timestep t and the class/text c (or null) are summed into one vector, cond = t_embed + c_embed, then poured through a small MLP that emits the block's adaptive dials — (γ1, β1, α1) for the attention sub-layer, (γ2, β2, α2) for the MLP sub-layer, regenerated fresh for every (t, c). Panel (b): adaLN keeps LayerNorm's exact formula, gamma * normalize(x) + beta, but now γ widens the standardized signal and β shifts its center on command from the conditioning. Panel (c) is the '-Zero': every α gate starts at zero, so at initialization each branch contributes times zero and the block is pure identity (x to x). Training then learns the alphas upward, fading each block in one at a time — so a newborn hundred-block DiT is a stable pass-through, and depth is earned rather than fought from the first step.
